previous_reply_acts.text:
(what I did)
- Fast-forwarded futon3c master to `f7ba3a34`. The branch's tests pass: 33 tests, 65 assertions, run in a separate process.
- Wrote the probe `holes/labs/M-diagramprover/cascade_glue_probe.clj` (commit `49ed39cb`). Run it with `clojure -M holes/labs/M-diagramprover/cascade_glue_probe.clj`.
- Each pattern becomes one small model that owns its unit: "unit X holds if pattern X was applied and its prerequisites hold".
- The shared JVM hasn't loaded the new namespaces. They only matter there once something live calls them.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(findings, in more detail)
1. **Cycle refusal.** Reload supports ground control, but ground control has to come before reload. Joining the two orders therefore gives `:cycle` on ground and reload. The two relations have to stay as two models of the same patterns; merging them into one model doesn't work.
2. **Meets.** For both declared overlaps (ground/heartbeat meeting at event, envelope/reload meeting at seam), the declared meet is exactly what both sides depend on, excluding the pair themselves. That is Alexander's overlap. In the order itself, though, heartbeat sits below ground and reload sits below envelope, so the order-theoretic meet is heartbeat and reload. In this exemplar, "meet" means the shared dependency, not the lattice meet. That's worth stating wherever the semilattice claim is made.
3. **Knock-outs.** These are counterfactuals of the form "had pattern P not been applied, what fails?", and the two readings give different answers:
   - Under precedence, dropping seam fails everything, and reload depends on all five other patterns.
   - Under support, dropping event fails envelope, ground and heartbeat but not reload.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(limits)
- The equation grammar takes only two operands, so I chained helper variables for patterns with several prerequisites.
- Two producers of one token didn't come up here, because every unit has a single owner. Real cascades will need the OR rule.
- Predictions are counted with conditioning on at most one variable, so the count is truncated.
- Values are true/false only. Nothing here touches G.
- I haven't run it on the peripheral sensitivity exemplar. Its cascade graphs are only in Lean (`PeripheralCascadePolicies.lean`), not in EDN.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (next) The step from here to the War Machine is the run I offered last time: one recorded click's R6 interpretations, joined the same way, with the OR rule added. That would test whether the fit holds on real cascades and not only on hand-written ones.
